question: Explain the core advantages of Spring Boot over standard Spring Framework (Auto-Configuration, Starters, Embedded Servers).
idealAnswer: Spring Boot eliminates boilerplate XML/Java configuration through Auto-Configuration (@EnableAutoConfiguration), bundled Starter POMs (spring-boot-starter-web), and embedded servers (Tomcat/Jetty) for standalone JAR execution.
ideal_answer: Spring Boot eliminates boilerplate XML/Java configuration through Auto-Configuration (@EnableAutoConfiguration), bundled Starter POMs (spring-boot-starter-web), and embedded servers (Tomcat/Jetty) for standalone JAR execution.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Core Concepts and Spring Boot Core Advantages comprehension.

question: How does Spring Boot Auto-Configuration work under the hood using @EnableAutoConfiguration and META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports?
idealAnswer: Spring Boot scans auto-configuration classes listed in imports files. These classes use conditional annotations (@ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, @ConditionalOnProperty) to instantiate beans only if required libraries or custom beans are present.
ideal_answer: Spring Boot scans auto-configuration classes listed in imports files. These classes use conditional annotations (@ConditionalOnClass, @ConditionalOnMissingBean, @ConditionalOnProperty) to instantiate beans only if required libraries or custom beans are present.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Auto-Configuration and Auto-Configuration Mechanism comprehension.

question: What does @SpringBootApplication encapsulate (@Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, @ComponentScan)?
idealAnswer: @SpringBootApplication combines three annotations: @Configuration (marks class as bean source), @EnableAutoConfiguration (triggers auto-configuration), and @ComponentScan (scans packages for @Component, @Service, @Repository, @Controller).
ideal_answer: @SpringBootApplication combines three annotations: @Configuration (marks class as bean source), @EnableAutoConfiguration (triggers auto-configuration), and @ComponentScan (scans packages for @Component, @Service, @Repository, @Controller).
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Annotations and @SpringBootApplication Anatomy comprehension.

question: Explain Spring Boot Starter dependencies (e.g. spring-boot-starter-web, spring-boot-starter-data-jpa) and how they manage transitive versions.
idealAnswer: Starters aggregate curated sets of compatible transitive dependencies. Used alongside spring-boot-starter-parent, they manage dependency versions without requiring explicit version tags in pom.xml.
ideal_answer: Starters aggregate curated sets of compatible transitive dependencies. Used alongside spring-boot-starter-parent, they manage dependency versions without requiring explicit version tags in pom.xml.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Dependencies and Starters & Dependency Management comprehension.

question: Explain Spring Data JPA: JpaRepository, Query Methods by method names, and @Query (JPQL vs Native SQL).
idealAnswer: Spring Data JPA reduces boilerplate data access. JpaRepository provides CRUD and pagination out-of-the-box. Derived query methods generate queries from method names (findByEmailAndActive). @Query executes custom JPQL or native SQL.
ideal_answer: Spring Data JPA reduces boilerplate data access. JpaRepository provides CRUD and pagination out-of-the-box. Derived query methods generate queries from method names (findByEmailAndActive). @Query executes custom JPQL or native SQL.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Data Access and Spring Data JPA & Repositories comprehension.

question: What are Entity Relationships in JPA/Hibernate (@OneToOne, @OneToMany, @ManyToOne, @ManyToMany), and what is FetchType.LAZY vs EAGER?
idealAnswer: Relationships define cardinality between entities. FetchType.LAZY loads associated entities on demand when accessed (preventing massive queries). FetchType.EAGER joins and loads associations immediately.
ideal_answer: Relationships define cardinality between entities. FetchType.LAZY loads associated entities on demand when accessed (preventing massive queries). FetchType.EAGER joins and loads associations immediately.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Data Access & JPA and JPA Entity Relationships & Fetch Types comprehension.

question: How do you solve the N+1 Query Problem in Spring Data JPA using JOIN FETCH, @EntityGraph, or DTO Projections?
idealAnswer: The N+1 problem occurs when fetching N entities triggers N additional queries to load lazy relationships. It is solved using JPQL 'JOIN FETCH', @EntityGraph to define fetch plans, or constructor DTO projections.
ideal_answer: The N+1 problem occurs when fetching N entities triggers N additional queries to load lazy relationships. It is solved using JPQL 'JOIN FETCH', @EntityGraph to define fetch plans, or constructor DTO projections.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Performance & JPA and N+1 Problem Resolution comprehension.

question: Explain Exception Handling in Spring Boot REST APIs using @ControllerAdvice, @RestControllerAdvice, and @ExceptionHandler.

question: How does Bean Validation (Hibernate Validator) work in Spring Boot using @Valid, @NotNull, @Size, and custom ConstraintValidators?
idealAnswer: Spring Boot integrates Jakarta Bean Validation. Adding @Valid / @Validated on controller request bodies validates model annotations (@NotNull, @Email, @Size). Custom validators implement ConstraintValidator<Annotation, Type>.

question: Explain Spring Security architecture in Spring Boot: SecurityFilterChain, AuthenticationManager, and UserDetailsService.
idealAnswer: Spring Security processes HTTP requests through a chain of filters (SecurityFilterChain). AuthenticationManager delegates credentials verification to AuthenticationProvider, which loads user details via UserDetailsService and validates passwords with PasswordEncoder.
ideal_answer: Spring Security processes HTTP requests through a chain of filters (SecurityFilterChain). AuthenticationManager delegates credentials verification to AuthenticationProvider, which loads user details via UserDetailsService and validates passwords with PasswordEncoder.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Security and Spring Security Architecture comprehension.

question: How do you implement Stateless JWT (JSON Web Token) Authentication and Authorization in Spring Boot 3?
idealAnswer: Create a custom OncePerRequestFilter that extracts the JWT token from the Authorization header, validates the signature, extracts username and roles, and sets an Authentication object in the SecurityContextHolder.
ideal_answer: Create a custom OncePerRequestFilter that extracts the JWT token from the Authorization header, validates the signature, extracts username and roles, and sets an Authentication object in the SecurityContextHolder.
explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Security and JWT Authentication in Spring Boot 3 comprehension.

question: How do you write Integration Tests in Spring Boot using @SpringBootTest, @WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest, and Testcontainers?
idealAnswer: @SpringBootTest loads full ApplicationContext for end-to-end integration tests. Test slices (@WebMvcTest for controllers with MockMvc, @DataJpaTest for repositories) load minimal contexts for fast unit testing. Testcontainers runs real Docker databases during tests.

explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Testing and Spring Boot Testing Slices comprehension.

question: What is Spring Boot Native Compilation with GraalVM (AOT processing), and what are the benefits for startup time and memory footprint?
idealAnswer: Spring Boot 3 supports ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation with GraalVM Native Image. It precomputes reflection and bean definitions at build time, generating standalone native binaries with sub-second startup times and minuscule memory footprint.

explanation: Evaluates Spring Boot Modern Spring Boot and Spring Boot GraalVM Native Image comprehension.
